result:
**Construction.** Let φ = (1+√5)/2 and define x_n = 3·{nφ}, where {·} is the fractional part. Then 0 ≤ x_n < 3, so the sequence is bounded.

**Verification.**

1. Take i ≠ j and set d = |i−j| ≥ 1. Since {iφ} − {jφ} ≡ (i−j)φ (mod 1), the difference {iφ} − {jφ} differs from (i−j)φ by an integer. Hence |{iφ} − {jφ}| ≥ ‖dφ‖, where ‖·‖ denotes the distance to the nearest integer.

2. φ is badly approximable, because its continued fraction is [1;1,1,…]. Its conjugate is −1/φ, so for any integer p and q ≥ 1,
 |q²−pq−p²| ≥ 1 (this is the norm form of ℤ[φ], and it is nonzero).
 Suppose |qφ−p| < 1/(3q), and write δ = qφ−p. Then q²−pq−p² = (qφ−p)(q+p−qφ+... ), and the second factor is of size about q√5. This gives |norm| ≈ √5·q·|δ| < √5/3 < 1, which contradicts |norm| ≥ 1.
 Hence ‖dφ‖ ≥ 1/(3d) for all d ≥ 1.

3. Therefore |x_i − x_j| = 3|{iφ} − {jφ}| ≥ 3·1/(3d) = 1/d. Since a > 1 and d ≥ 1, we have d^{−a} ≤ d^{−1}, so
 |x_i − x_j|·|i−j|^a ≥ (1/d)·d^a = d^{a−1} ≥ 1.

This holds for every pair of distinct nonnegative integers i, j, so the sequence satisfies the condition.

ANSWER: $x_n = 3\{n\varphi\}$ with $\varphi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}$ (fractional part), which is bounded and satisfies $|x_i-x_j||i-j|^a\ge1$.
